fields.hero_prompt: Build a MaxDiff survey that ranks the 16 features on my app's roadmap.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a maxdiff survey?

plan.angle: The top 10 is definitions and analysis explainers from research-software vendors: what best-worst scaling is, how counts work, why it beats rating scales. None shows a finished MaxDiff survey with its design numbers and its readout together. This page shows four MaxDiff surveys built from a prompt, each with its item count, items per question and question count stated so the 3-showings rule is visible, each ending in a decision read from best-minus-worst scores, and the how-to and FAQ give the sourced sizing rules (about 15 to 40 items, 4 or 5 per question, each item shown 3 times) and how to read a score.
tab_stories: Taskwren, a project management app, shows 420 users its 16 roadmap features 4 at a time over 12 questions; offline mode is picked best in 46% of its showings and worst in 9% for a score of +37, dark mode scores -26, and the team builds offline mode first.

Larchmint Skincare tests 10 claims for a new moisturizer jar with 600 shoppers, 5 claims per question over 6 questions; fragrance free scores +41, made in Vermont scores -36, the results post to the #brand-team channel in Slack, and fragrance free goes on the front of the jar.
Sundergate Summit asks 350 registered attendees to choose among 12 session topics on their phones, 4 topics per screen over 9 screens; pricing workshops score +44 and get the main hall.

Pennacombe Kitchens asks 500 loyalty members about 15 dishes, 5 per question over 9 questions; any dish scoring below -20 is flagged and the head chef gets an email, and lamb tagine at -24 and veal liver at -41 come off the spring menu.
